You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

How to work, in every instance (follow this exactly): keep a program library in the folder /home/ubuntu/continual-arc-baselines/.workbench/runs/adhoc-openclawlearner-1790687857/attempts/d3ae97d7f78548fbbe6aa9202f4eeb9d/system/state/workspace/programs, one Python file per task, named for its task id (/home/ubuntu/continual-arc-baselines/.workbench/runs/adhoc-openclawlearner-1790687857/attempts/d3ae97d7f78548fbbe6aa9202f4eeb9d/system/state/workspace/programs/<task id>.py), defining transform(grid), which takes an input grid as a list of lists of integers and returns the output grid.
1. When an instance starts, look for the task's file. If it exists, run its transform on the test input and submit the result before anything else.
2. If there is no file, or its answer was wrong, request demonstration pairs as you judge necessary, write or fix transform, and run it on every pair you have received until it reproduces all of them; then submit its output for the test input. Checking a program on the pairs is free.
3. Submit only grids that your program produced.
4. After the verdict, save the program that reproduced all the pairs to the task's file, replacing any older version, then finish.

name: continual-arc
description: Solve Continual-ARC task instances with persistent per-task Python transforms, demos, and verified submissions.
---

# Continual ARC

For Continual-ARC instances that provide a task id, test grid, demonstrations, and a persistent program library:

1. At instance start, inspect `programs/<task id>.py`. If it exists, run its `transform(test_grid)` and submit that exact result before any other task action, as required by the instance protocol.
2. If the file is absent or that submission is judged incorrect, inspect every demo for common structure before requesting more. For divided panels, identify the uniform separator orientation, panel bounds, shared/rare colors, and exact cellwise relationship. Request a demo only when the new pair can distinguish competing rules; after each pair, test candidate rules against all examples. Do not infer a rule from a single appealing coincidence or proceed with a succession of unsupported submissions.
3. Implement `transform(grid)` only when the rule is supported, then run it on every demonstrated input. Compare full grids, including dimensions, colors, and unchanged cells; revise until all pairs match. Before submitting, validate the exact transform result is a nonempty rectangular grid with 1–30 rows and columns and integer cells 0–9; construct the action grid from that result rather than retyping it. Submit only after the program reproduces every available pair. If the demo cap arrives without a rule that reproduces the pairs, be explicit internally that it remains uncertain; make at most an evidence-based attempt within the limit, validating its grid.
4. On every instance turn, follow its response protocol exactly: one action per turn and exactly one action JSON object on the final line. Never hand-construct a submission independently of the executed transform.
5. After a correct verdict, ensure the reproduced transform is saved at `programs/<task id>.py`, then finish the instance. Do not mark an unverified transform as validated or overwrite a useful implementation with a guess. After an incorrect verdict, treat it as evidence against the tested rule: revisit the demos and correct the transform before another submission; do not repeat the same output or change colors/dimensions speculatively. Save a learned implementation only after it reproduces every demo.
